task_instance: Run the skill's step-by-step device-info capture script (model, L4T release, nvpmodel power mode, kernel, uptime, OS version) on this sandbox to produce the baseline report described in the skill's Output format section.
blocker_detail: The skill's own stated prerequisite is 'Running on a Jetson target (not the host PC)'. This developer-sandbox runtime is an x86_64 Linux VM (uname -m = x86_64), not an NVIDIA Jetson ARM device. Verified /proc/device-tree/model does not exist (cat: No such file or directory) and /etc/nv_tegra_release does not exist, confirming there is no Jetson hardware/device-tree present. The skill itself instructs exiting early with 'Not running on a Jetson target' in this exact situation. Per the task's safety rules, I did not fabricate or stub the device-tree files, nvpmodel binary, or L4T release data to fake a Jetson environment -- doing so would only produce fabricated output, not a real verified deliverable. Accomplishing the skill's core intent requires actual (or physically/console-accessed) Jetson hardware, which no shell/file/web tool in this runtime can provide.
evidence: Commands run in work directory: `cat /proc/device-tree/model` -> 'No such file or directory'; `uname -a` -> 'Linux vm 6.18.44-fc-v37 ... x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux'; `ls /etc/nv_tegra_release` -> 'No such file or directory'; `which nvpmodel` -> not found. These confirm the sandbox is a generic x86_64 VM with none of the Jetson-specific filesystem artifacts (device-tree, L4T release file) or the nvpmodel binary that the skill depends on, and there is no Jetson target reachable via SSH or otherwise in this environment.
